  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main
      - 'epic/**'

  contents: read

  group: ci-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  release-version-integrity:
    name: Release version integrity
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&
      github.actor == 'github-actions[bot]' &&
      github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'github-actions[bot]' &&
      github.event.pull_request.base.ref == github.event.repository.default_branch &&
      github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository &&
      startsWith(github.event.pull_request.head.ref, 'release/v')
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read

    steps:
      - name: Check out trusted release validation
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          persist-credentials: false
          sparse-checkout: |-
            scripts/validate-release-pr.mts
            scripts/release-github-evidence.mts
          sparse-checkout-cone-mode: false

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          package-manager-cache: false

      - name: Validate version-only release change
        env:
          GITHUB_DEFAULT_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          RELEASE_PR_HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          RELEASE_PR_MODE: pre-merge
          RELEASE_PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: node scripts/validate-release-pr.mts

  verify:
    name: Verification (Linux)
    needs: release-version-integrity
    if: always() && needs.release-version-integrity.result == 'skipped'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
      issues: read
      pull-requests: read

    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # Architecture validates the exact event base/head and accepted epic history.
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          package-manager-cache: false

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run policy, type, and test verification
        env:
          HVIR_REPO_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: npm run verify

  electron-smoke:
    name: Electron smoke (Linux)
    needs: release-version-integrity
    if: always() && needs.release-version-integrity.result == 'skipped'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15

    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          package-manager-cache: false

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run production Electron workflow
        env:
          HVIR_SMOKE_ARTIFACT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/hvir-smoke-artifacts/production

        env:

        with:

          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/hvir-smoke-artifacts
          if-no-files-found: ignore

+# hvir
+
+**hvir** is a lightweight, view-first workbench for agentic development. It brings
+terminals, project files, Git, document review, web panes, and agent sessions into one
+Electron desktop application.
+
+## Features
+
+- Work with local projects or connect to projects over SSH.
+- Run multiple terminal workspaces with split panes, search, themes, and session
+  recovery.
+- Browse, edit, preview, diff, and review project files, including Markdown and
+  rendered documents.
+- Inspect Git status, history, branches, changes, and worktrees.
+- Monitor agent sessions and usage from supported harnesses, including Claude Code,
+  Codex, Cursor, Gemini, GitHub Copilot, Pi, and shell sessions.
+- Open project web panes and manage workspace-specific settings.
+- Package native macOS and Linux desktop applications with Electron Builder.
+
+## Requirements
+
+- Node.js 24 or newer
+- npm
+- Git
+- A supported desktop environment:
+  - macOS (Apple Silicon packaging is configured)
+  - Linux (x64 and arm64 Debian packaging is configured)
+
+SSH projects additionally require access to the target host through the local SSH
+configuration and credentials.
+
+## Getting started
+
+Clone the repository, install dependencies, and start the development application:
+
+```bash
+git clone https://github.com/jarmak-personal/hvir.git
+cd hvir
+npm ci
+npm run dev
+```
+
+The install step also installs Electron's runtime and rebuilds the native modules
+required by the terminal and file-operation features.
+
+## Common commands
+
+| Command | Description |
+| --- | --- |
+| `npm run dev` | Start the Electron application in development mode |
+| `npm run build` | Type-check and create a production application build |
+| `npm run preview` | Preview the built application |
+| `npm test` | Run the Vitest test suite |
+| `npm run lint` | Run ESLint |
+| `npm run format:check` | Check formatting with Prettier |
+| `npm run verify` | Run seam, ADR, architecture, lint, type-check, and unit-test checks |
+| `npm run smoke` | Build and run the production Electron smoke scenarios |
+| `npm run build:dir` | Build and assemble an unpacked Electron application |
+| `npm run pack:mac:arm64` | Build a macOS arm64 package |
+| `npm run pack:linux:x64` | Build a Linux x64 Debian package |
+| `npm run pack:linux:arm64` | Build a Linux arm64 Debian package |
+
+For a focused smoke test, use `npm run smoke:scenario -- <scenario-name>`. The
+repository also provides platform-specific smoke and SSH acceptance commands in
+`package.json`.
+
+## Project layout
+
+```text
+src/main/       Electron main-process services and native integrations
+src/preload/    Secure bridge between Electron and the renderer
+src/renderer/   React workbench UI
+src/shared/     Types and contracts shared across processes
+scripts/        Development, architecture, smoke, and release tooling
+test/           Unit, integration, and contract tests
+build/          Application icons, entitlements, and packaging resources
+```
+
+The main process owns filesystem, Git, SSH, terminal, and Electron operations. The
+renderer presents those capabilities through explicit IPC contracts.

+**hvir** is a lightweight, view-first workbench for agentic development. It brings
